exam.title: JSA Certified Associate JavaScript Programmer
exam.study_prerequisites: No formal certification prerequisite is published; JSE-40-01 knowledge is recommended. Practice implementing and debugging JavaScript objects, prototypes, classes, built-in collections, closures, generators, promises, async/await, and network requests. Predict identity, receiver, mutation, iteration, and asynchronous outcomes before running each example, and verify the active exam version before purchase.

review.notes: All 40 named JSA-41-01 objectives are mapped through object identity and copying, property and prototype mechanics, class construction/inheritance/statics, every named built-in collection/API, closures/context/decorators/iteration, promise combinators, async/await, XMLHttpRequest and Fetch. Three integrated scenarios, eight labs and 40 original checks are included. Modern related context is separated from the published scope, and O'Reilly/Udemy are automation-blocked rather than missing. No recalled/live item, answer dump or copied course question is used.

findings.title: Forty objectives require concrete code evidence
findings.evidence: The four groups cover object mechanics, built-ins and asynchronous HTTP; prior scenarios were short sketches.
findings.recommendation: Add seven verified public blocks,143 core + 84 scenario checks in both runtimes and36 browser API/UI checks; improve all 40 answers and retain eight broader activities as proposed.
findings.resolution: Add seven verified public blocks,143 core + 84 scenario checks in both runtimes and36 browser API/UI checks; improve all 40 answers and retain eight broader activities as proposed.

findings.title: Descriptor defaults depend on whether the property exists
findings.evidence: New omitted flags default false; omitted attributes of an existing property retain their values. One source example obscures this distinction.
findings.recommendation: Correct teaching/answer 6, test new versus existing flags, conflicting descriptor kinds, non-configurable writes and final writable lock.
findings.resolution: Correct teaching/answer 6, test new versus existing flags, conflicting descriptor kinds, non-configurable writes and final writable lock.

findings.title: Shallow copying also invokes behavior and can partially mutate
findings.evidence: Source getters, target assignment setters and preceding writes remain observable when a later assign write fails.
findings.recommendation: Explain values versus descriptors, spread differences, nested aliases and null-prototype dictionaries; execute original boundary probes.
findings.resolution: Explain values versus descriptors, spread differences, nested aliases and null-prototype dictionaries; execute original boundary probes.

findings.title: Sparse slots differ from explicit undefined values
findings.evidence: Map and several predicates skip holes, find visits them and spread materializes undefined; callback index affects parseInt.
findings.recommendation: Teach method-specific contracts and execute sparse/empty arrays, sort/reduce and explicit conversion callbacks.
findings.resolution: Teach method-specific contracts and execute sparse/empty arrays, sort/reduce and explicit conversion callbacks.

findings.title: Successful parsing does not establish an application-valid record
findings.evidence: Blank numeric text coerces to zero, dates can normalize and JSON accepts primitives/loses unsupported values.
findings.recommendation: Build strict decimal/date/row validation with bounded totals, first-valid duplicate policy and diagnostics; test original fixtures and exact public code.
findings.resolution: Build strict decimal/date/row validation with bounded totals, first-valid duplicate policy and diagnostics; test original fixtures and exact public code.

findings.title: Empty promise combinators and cancellation are distinct
findings.evidence: All([]) fulfills, any([]) rejects and race([]) stays pending; settling an aggregate does not cancel its other operations.
findings.recommendation: Add empty/failure/order/finally/async traces and actual AbortController/XHR timeout tests with synthetic browser responses.
findings.resolution: Add empty/failure/order/finally/async traces and actual AbortController/XHR timeout tests with synthetic browser responses.

findings.title: HTTP success, body parsing andschema validity require separate checks
findings.evidence: Fetch resolves on HTTP errors; XHR load is not an HTTP success guarantee; body use/cancellation/errors differ.
findings.recommendation: Add complete Fetch/XHR clients andsafe-text retry UI; test 36 browser cases including status, syntax, shape, timeout, abort andloading/recovery.
findings.resolution: Add complete Fetch/XHR clients andsafe-text retry UI; test 36 browser cases including status, syntax, shape, timeout, abort andloading/recovery.

import hashlib,json,re
from pathlib import Path
from playwright.sync_api import sync_playwright
R=Path(__file__).resolve().parents[1];o=R/'.maintenance/deep-jsa-41-01-2026-09-29'
guide=(R/'guides/JSA-41-01-certified-associate-javascript-programmer.md').read_text(encoding='utf-8')
blocks=re.findall(r'```javascript\n(.*?)```',guide,re.S);assert len(blocks)==7
receipt=json.loads((o/'local-checks.json').read_text(encoding='utf-8'));assert receipt['passed']
for index,name in enumerate(['core','catalog','normalize','client'],3):
    assert blocks[index]==(o/f'{name}.js').read_text(encoding='utf-8')
    assert hashlib.sha256(blocks[index].encode()).hexdigest()==receipt['source_sha256'][name]
results=[]
with sync_playwright() as p:
    browser=p.chromium.launch(channel='chrome',headless=True)
    for index in range(3):
        page=browser.new_page();events=[];errors=[]
        page.on('console',lambda msg:events.append(msg.text));page.on('pageerror',lambda e:errors.append(str(e)))
        page.add_script_tag(content=blocks[index])
        if index==0:
            result=page.evaluate('[product.id,product.details.stock,product[field],Object.keys(product)]')
            assert result==['A1',4,12.5,['id','details','unit-price']] and len(events)==3
        elif index==1:
            result=page.evaluate('() => {const a=Account.from({owner:"A",balance:10});a.deposit(3);return [a.available,a.currency,a.owner,Object.hasOwn(a,"deposit"),typeof Account.from];}')
            assert result==[13,'USD','A',False,'function']
        else:
            result=page.evaluate('() => {const a=new Account("A");return [a.describe(),Object.getPrototypeOf(a)===Account.prototype,Object.hasOwn(a,"describe")];}')
            assert result==['A',True,False]
        assert not errors
        results.append(dict(block_index=index,result=result,console=events,errors=errors,passed=True));page.close()
    browser.close()
receipt['public_example_sha256']=[hashlib.sha256(b.encode()).hexdigest() for b in blocks]
receipt['public_code_blocks']=7;receipt['introductory_blocks']=results
(o/'local-checks.json').write_text(json.dumps(receipt,indent=2,ensure_ascii=False)+'\n',encoding='utf-8')
print('All seven exact public blocks verified; three introductory examples also executed in isolated Chrome pages.')

groups.title: Block 1: Classless Objects — 11 items, 25%
objectives: 1.1 Create and initialize objects with object-literal syntax.
1.2 Add, change, remove, and safely access ordinary and nested properties.
1.3 Select dot or bracket notation for ordinary, multi-word, dynamic, and computed keys.
1.4 Test property presence and enumerate own keys, values, and entries safely with in, for...in, and Object helpers.
1.5 Distinguish reference identity from structural or deep equivalence.
1.6 Explain reference copies; make shallow copies with Object.assign and spread; recognize deep-clone limitations.
1.7 Define object methods and reason correctly about this at the call site.
1.8 Define getters and setters that compute or validate state.
1.9 Configure property descriptors and apply preventExtensions, seal, and freeze.
1.10 Create objects through factories, constructor functions with new, and Object.create.
1.11 Explain the prototype chain and work with [[Prototype]], Function.prototype, and Object.setPrototypeOf.

groups.title: Block 2: Classes and Class-Based Approach — 7 items, 23%
objectives: 2.1 Declare classes and class expressions with constructors, fields, and methods; treat classes as values.
2.2 Instantiate classes with new and test prototype relationships with instanceof.
2.3 Initialize class fields in constructors or with field declarations.
2.4 Define computed or validated class state with getters and setters.
2.5 Implement inheritance and overriding with extends and super.
2.6 Define and call static properties and methods on the class.
2.7 Relate class syntax to constructor functions and prototype methods.

groups.title: Block 3: Built-in Objects — 12 items, 27%
objectives: 3.1 Convert, validate, and format numeric values with Number APIs.
3.2 Transform, split, search, replace, pad, trim, and compare strings.
3.3 Construct and modify Date values, distinguish local time from UTC, and measure elapsed time.
3.4 Create, merge, add, remove, slice, splice, spread, destructure, and iterate arrays.
3.5 Apply find, every, some, filter, sort, map, and reduce with correct callback behavior.
3.6 Create and manipulate Set collections and iterate their unique values.
3.7 Create and manipulate Map collections and iterate key-value entries.
3.8 Use plain objects as dictionary-like data structures.
3.9 Serialize supported JavaScript data to JSON and parse JSON text.
3.10 Apply common Math constants and functions for rounding, random values, ranges, powers, logs, and trigonometry.
3.11 Create regular expressions and use test, exec, match, search, and replace.
3.12 Explain how built-in prototypes can be extended and why doing so is risky.

groups.title: Block 4: Advanced Functions — 10 items, 25%
objectives: 4.1 Use default and rest parameters, spread arguments, destructuring, and object-based named-parameter patterns.
4.2 Explain lexical closures and create immediately invoked function expressions.
4.3 Control call context and forward arguments with call, apply, and bind.
4.4 Build decorators and higher-order functions that accept or return functions.
4.5 Create generators, iterators, and custom iterable objects.
4.6 Organize asynchronous callback flows and propagate errors deliberately.
4.7 Create promises and handle fulfillment, rejection, and cleanup with then, catch, and finally.
4.8 Chain promises and coordinate work with Promise.all, Promise.any, and Promise.race.
4.9 Write async functions, await promises, and handle asynchronous errors with try/catch.
4.10 Make asynchronous HTTP requests with XMLHttpRequest and Fetch.
